title: GTA-5: A Unified Graph Transformer Framework for Ligands and Protein Binding Sites — Part I: Constructing the PDB Pocket and Ligand Space
authors: Bogdan C. Ciambur; Raphaël Pageau; Olivier Sperandio
one_liner_zh: 该文提出统一图Transformer自编码器GTA-5，将配体与蛋白结合口袋编码为三维点云嵌入空间，虽非典型TF-DNA体系，但蛋白-DNA结合位点建模与口袋表征方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Structural recognition between a protein target and a ligand underpins therapeutic innovation, yet computational representations of protein binding sites and small molecules remain largely disjoint. Here we introduce GTA-5, a unified graph transformer auto-encoder framework designed to capture the geometric structure and chemical composition of ligands and protein binding pockets, embedding them into multidimensional latent spaces where proximity reflects functional compatibility. Ligands and pockets are represented as three-dimensional point clouds annotated with Tripos atom type labels, omitting explicit bond connectivity to enable structural reasoning based on spatial context rather than predefined connectivity graphs. By not enforcing bond topology, GTA-5 maintains representational flexibility across molecular modalities while preserving chemically meaningful local environments. The model was trained on a curated dataset from the Protein Data Bank comprising 64,124 liganded pockets and 23,133 unique ligands spanning 2,257 protein families. We find that functional protein families cluster coherently in both pocket and ligand latent spaces while retaining biologically meaningful heterogeneity. The model captures physicochemical pocket properties such as volume, exposure, and hydrophobicity directly from raw structural data, while ligands with distinct scaffolds co-localise when occupying similar binding environments. This provides a basis for several downstream applications including scaffold hopping in ligand-based virtual screening, QSAR/QSPR modelling using embedding-derived descriptors, and drug repurposing via pocket similarity. More broadly, the GTA-5 framework establishes a foundation for structural reasoning across molecular modalities in drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质靶标与配体之间的结构识别是治疗创新的基础，然而蛋白质结合位点和小分子的计算表示在很大程度上仍相互脱节。在此，我们引入GTA-5，一个统一的图变换器自编码器框架，旨在捕捉配体和蛋白质结合口袋的几何结构与化学组成，将其嵌入多维潜在空间，其中邻近性反映功能兼容性。配体和口袋被表示为带有Tripos原子类型标签的三维点云，省略显式键连接，以便基于空间上下文而非预定义连接图进行结构推理。通过不强制键拓扑，GTA-5在保持化学意义上局部环境的同时，跨分子模态维持表示灵活性。该模型在来自蛋白质数据银行（Protein Data Bank）的精选数据集上训练，包含64,124个配体结合口袋和23,133个独特配体，涵盖2,257个蛋白质家族。我们发现，功能蛋白质家族在口袋和配体潜在空间中均聚类一致，同时保留具有生物学意义的异质性。该模型直接从原始结构数据中捕捉口袋的物理化学性质，如体积、暴露度和疏水性，而具有不同骨架的配体在占据相似结合环境时共定位。这为若干下游应用提供了基础，包括基于配体的虚拟筛选中的骨架跳跃、使用嵌入衍生描述符的QSAR/QSPR建模，以及通过口袋相似性进行的药物重定位。更广泛地，GTA-5框架为药物发现中跨分子模态的结构推理奠定了基础。
